requested_order.text: Wegovy (semaglutide) 0.25 mg SC once weekly x4 weeks, then titrate per label to 2.4 mg weekly

weight_management_program.text:
A/P:
1. Obesity, BMI 33.3 — plan starting today:
 - Reduced-calorie meal plan of about 1600 kcal/day with food logging in a phone app.
 - Gym sessions, treadmill + light weights, 4 days a week (~150 min/week).
 - Referred to a dietitian-led weight management program.
 Follow-up in ~3 months.
2. Low back pain — mechanical; core strengthening at gym; ibuprofen PRN sparingly.
3. Anxiety — stable on sertraline.

NUTRITION CONSULT — INITIAL
Date: 02/07/2026
Dietitian-led weight management program intake. Food log: regular meals, but 500–700 kcal of afternoon grazing (crackers, cheese, trail mix) while working from home.
Plan: ~1600 kcal/day, logged in phone app; scheduled 3 PM snack (≤200 kcal, pre-portioned); keep snack foods out of the office; high-fiber lunch.
Activity: gym 4 days/week, treadmill + light weights, ~150 min/week.
RD follow-up in 4–6 weeks.

PRIMARY CARE PROGRESS NOTE
Date: 05/03/2026
S: Weight follow-up. Continues the meal plan and gym routine she started in January; logging in the app most days, gym 3–4 days/week. Good adherence most weeks. Back pain better with strengthening.
O: Wt 84.5 kg, BMI 33.0. BP 119/69.
A/P:
1. Obesity — continue program and RD visits.
2. Low back pain — improved.

PRIMARY CARE PROGRESS NOTE
Date: 08/08/2026
S: Weight follow-up. Continues the diet and exercise plan and program follow-ups since January — logging meals, gym 4 days a week. Frustrated: weight 83.2 kg today vs 85.3 kg in January when she started (-2.5%), stuck for the last couple of months despite reported adherence. Wants to discuss medication. No MTC/MEN2 history, no pancreatitis, no gallbladder disease. Tubal ligation.
O: Wt 83.2 kg, BMI 32.5. BP 116/69.

A/P:
1. Obesity, BMI 32.5 — plateau on lifestyle program. Start semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly (Wegovy) with standard dose titration; counseled on GI side effects and hydration. Continue diet/gym plan. Recheck in 3 months.
2. Migraine — note possible nausea overlap; continue sumatriptan PRN.

OUTSIDE RECORDS — SCANNED — 03/01/2025
Source: Evergreen Family Dentistry
Medical clearance form for two crown preparations under local anesthesia. Current meds listed: sertraline, omeprazole, sumatriptan PRN, vitamin D. No cardiac or bleeding history, no bisphosphonate use. Cleared for dental procedure, no restrictions. Signed and returned.

PHARMACIST MEDICATION REVIEW — 03/16/2025
Pt asked whether she can take St. John's wort and a magnesium supplement for mood/headaches. Advised AGAINST St. John's wort with sertraline and sumatriptan (serotonin syndrome risk, and it reduces effectiveness of many meds). Magnesium oxide 400 mg daily is reasonable for migraine prevention; may cause loose stools. Pt will skip St. John's wort.

Early-season influenza vaccine administered per pt request before travel (0.5 mL IM R deltoid). VIS reviewed. No reaction after 15 min observation.
